title: Winey Gooey Mexican Chicken Pozole
description: A rich and comforting norteño-style Mexican stew featuring tender chicken, creamy rice, and a hint of wine. Perfect for a chilly evening, this dish is easy to make in large batches for a fun gathering around the lazy Susan spinner.
instructions: In a large Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons of oil over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the pot and set aside. Add the onion and garlic to the pot and cook until the onion is translucent, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper to the pot and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken broth and white wine to the pot and bring to a simmer.
Return the chicken to the pot and cook until the meat is tender and the liquid has reduced slightly, about 20-25 minutes.
While the chicken cooks, prepare the rice according to package instructions. Fluff the cooked rice with a fork and set aside.
Once the chicken is cooked, remove it from the pot and shred it into bite-sized pieces.
Add the cooked rice to the pot and stir to combine.
Stir in the shredded cheese until melted and well combined.
Serve the pozole hot, garnished with additional shredded cheese, diced onion, and a sprinkle of paprika, if desired.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
